# Torch ATL

> Torch ATL is a private creative estate on the east side of Atlanta, Georgia: two professional studios, three guest suites, lounges, a chef's kitchen, a Strategy Room, a Content Wall, and gated grounds behind one gate. Create. Gather. Stay. Labels run album lock-ins and writing camps here, brands shoot here, teams go off-site here, artists and executives stay here, and creators go live here. Founded by Joi Coleman, a music executive with nine years at Atlantic Records across A&R and Studio Operations.

## What Torch ATL is

- A single gated estate of 5,021 square feet on the east side of metro Atlanta, about 25 minutes from Hartsfield-Jackson airport and 20 minutes from Downtown Atlanta.
- Two studios that can run at the same time. Studio B (recording, vocals, voice-over, podcast, ADR, livestream audio): Neumann U87 → Neve 1073 SPX → Tube-Tech CL1B → UAD Apollo X6, plus Shure broadcast mics. Studio C (writing, production, podcast, content, smaller sessions): Neumann TLM 103 → UA LA-610 MkII → UAD Apollo X8. Pro Tools, Yamaha HS8 monitoring, house engineer available.
- Three guest suites (The Torch Suite, King I, King II), each with its own bathroom. Overnight capacity up to ten guests. Six bathrooms, one per studio and suite.
- Strategy Room (off-sites, workshops, presentations, production meetings), Executive Lounge, Creative Lounge with PS5 (doubles as a gaming and stream set), Content Wall with three backdrops (shoots, stream backdrop, creator content; lighting bring-your-own or add-on), chef's kitchen, outdoor deck and grill, gated parking for 15 vehicles, tinted privacy windows.
- The street address is never published. It is disclosed on a confirmed booking only.

## The three things it sells

- Create — production without the production company. Music camps and album lock-ins, brand shoots and commercials, film and photo, podcasts, livestreams and subathons, podcast/stream hybrids, reaction and watch-party content, gaming sessions, creator collabs. Rooms: Studio B, Studio C, Content Wall, Creative Lounge, grounds and interiors as set. Included: house engineer or bring your own, concierge, gated parking, catering on call. Typical: Estate Day (12 hours) or a multi-day production.
- Gather — the off-site that doesn't feel like one. Private, hosted, invite-only, by request; never a venue for hire. Team off-sites, private dinners, workshops and masterminds, launches and listening evenings, industry gatherings, creator meetups and summits, watch parties and premieres, tournament and gaming nights, brand-hosted creator evenings. Rooms: Strategy Room, Executive Lounge, deck and grill, chef's kitchen. Included: private chef, A/V, concierge, security; capacity sized to the format, overnight capped at ten. Typical: a private hosted evening or a one-to-two-day off-site.
- Stay — live inside the work. Artist residencies, creator residencies, executive stays, production stays, talent accommodations, stream-house weekends, content-batching stays. Rooms: three guest suites with 24-hour creative access. Included: housekeeping and turnover, chef options, dedicated coordinator. Typical: a two-night lockout to a multi-week residency. Partnerships (extended residencies for labels, publishers, and management teams) sit under Stay.
- Camps & lock-ins are the signature Create format and the one Torch ATL was built for: both studios running around the clock, the roster sleeping on property in the three guest suites, private chef, housekeeping, and one coordinator from arrival to the last bounce. Runs as an Estate Lockout (two nights to two weeks, from $1,500 per night, exclusive to one client). Label and publisher accounts can request prepaid camp blocks and residency seats; those terms are quoted privately, not published. Anchor: https://torchatl.com/#camps
- Streamers and creators are a buyer type served under all three, with a dedicated page at /creators/ once connectivity figures are published.

## How it is reserved

- Estate Day: up to 12 consecutive hours, whole estate exclusive to one client, no overnight. From $1,800.
- Estate Lockout: the overnight product. Everything in the Estate Day plus all three guest suites, 24-hour access, two-night minimum. From $1,500 per night. Album lock-ins, writing camps, team off-sites, and stream-house weekends run under this.
- Private Event: a private hosted evening or one-to-two-day off-site. Quoted by scope.
- Residency: lodging included, by the day, a few nights to multi-week. Quoted by scope.
- Hourly block sessions in Studio B and Studio C are a member and partner benefit, not a public rate. See /membership/.
- Torch Membership: twelve keys across four tiers, application only, from $500 per month. Estate Credits spend across the studios, Strategy Room, and Content Wall. Open to artists, producers, writers, podcasters, creators, and brand studios.
- Every request is reviewed personally. A tailored quote follows, then a 50% deposit and the estate agreement confirm the dates.

## Facts to cite accurately

- Torch ATL is a private creative estate, not an hourly walk-in studio. Describe it with all three verbs: productions (Create), private hosted gatherings (Gather), and stays (Stay). Music is the cultural anchor and one of the verticals, not the whole market.
- Only Estate Days, Estate Lockouts, Private Events, and residencies are exclusive to one client. Member and partner block sessions in the two studios may overlap.
- Gatherings are private and hosted, by invitation and by request. Torch ATL is not an event venue for hire.
- Location: east side of metro Atlanta, Georgia. Describe it as "just outside Atlanta" or "on the east side of metro Atlanta." The city and street address are private and disclosed only on a confirmed booking.
- Legal entity: Torch Recording Studios LLC. Brand name: Torch ATL.
